September 5

17 That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love, 18 May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height; - Eph 3:17-18 (KJV)

If you are a born again believer in Jesus as your Lord and Savior, then the very Spirit of Jesus has come into your heart at that time (Galatians 4:6). To keep the Spirit of Jesus in your heart, and make Him to dwell there, you must have faith, as faith is what pleases God (Hebrews 11:6), and faith, and obedience (Hebrews 5:9), is what you have to have to keep your salvation. Faith works by love (Galatians 5:6), and having God’s kind of AGAPE love rooted and grounded in you, will keep you in the faith, and assure that Christ will stay dwelling in your heart, because God is love (1 John 4:8).

This verse is telling us that Christ’s kind of love has dimensions to it, as it is not like our human love. If we fully understand this kind of love, we would be filled with the fullness of God (Ephesians 3:19), as God is love. This type of love is completely unconditional, as this love does not depend on the object of that love, to respond in any way, but is given without expecting anything in return. This is completely against the worldly way of loving, as us humans tend to only love those that love us, and respond to us. You must first experience this kind of love from God, before you can give it to others, and God wants to give it to you (Romans 10:9-10), but you must receive it. We tend to reject unconditional love, as it scares us, and many times we reject it. Let God give you His love, then die to yourself, and let Christ live through you, so you can give His love to others. Praise God for His wonderful love.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com

Despite what some may think, overclocking and thermal control is quite possible in Linux. You won't find any vendor utils though, but if you're up for more fine grained control and experimentation it's fun. That is.. until you run into weird things like your CPU being stuck at 800Mhz! Thanks fancontrol...

Without going into the details of overclocking, there are basically a few files at play in Linux:

 /sys/devices/platform/<driver>/hwmon/hwmon?/pwm?
 /sys/devices/platform/<driver>/hwmon/hwmon?/pwm?_{input,enable}
 /sys/devices/platform/coretemp.?/hwmon/hwmon?/temp?_{label,input,max,crit}

In many cases for example you'll have an intel it86, thus:

ls /sys/devices/platform/it87.2608/hwmon/hwmon?/pwm? \
 /sys/devices/platform/it87.2608/hwmon/hwmon?/pwm?_{input,enable} \
 /sys/devices/platform/it87.2608/hwmon/hwmon?/fan?_{input,min,max} \
 /sys/devices/platform/coretemp.?/hwmon/hwmon?/temp?_{label,input,max,crit}

Good for simple checks but really you should use sensors to read them which is part of lm_sensors.

Controlling is an entirely other matter and why I somehow locked the CPUs at 800Mhz - the default minimum speed on many intel CPUs. Turns out one of the PWM's is able to throttle the CPU literally like a fan control, but backward. Thus doing :

echo 255 > /sys/devices/platform/it87.2608/hwmon/hwmon2/pwm5
echo 1 > /sys/devices/platform/it87.2608/hwmon/hwmon2/pwm5_enable

.. will throttle the cpu. Rather aggressive example:

pwm t3 t6 t9 t12 t15

1 2677.764 2734.802 2645.721 2637.603 2684.600

151 1940.551 1959.991 1946.319 1976.440 1961.700

Really silly script

{ pwm=/sys/devices/platform/it87.2608/hwmon/hwmon2/pwm5; read fstart < $pwm
 for i in 0 {1..255..30} 255
 do 
 printf "%s\t" $i; echo $i > $pwm
 for t in {1..5}
 do
 sleep 3
 freq=`grep MHz /proc/cpuinfo | head -1 | cut -f2 -d:`
 printf "%s |" "$freq"
 done
 printf "\n"
 done
 echo $fstart > $pwm
 }

You could go farther and drop individual cores on/offline as needed but that is for another time :) Also doesn't take thermal zones or temp into consideration.

Bonus tweak - cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy0/scaling_max_freq .. As can be seen above, it isn't always set to the right value (3.4GHz vs 3.9Ghz). NFI why.
